title: Data Dignity declaration
description: Machine-validatable schema for /.well-known/data-dignity.json, format v0.5 only. The core grammar is CLOSED: unknown core members fail validation, and everything site-specific goes under 'extensions' (ignored when unrecognized) or 'custom_classes' (mapped to standard classes). Earlier formats are handled by a checker's version-security rules (LEGACY, not graded), never by this schema. Serialization rules the schema language cannot express are normative in SCHEMA.md: UTF-8 only, duplicate member names are rejection, bounded size/depth/string/array lengths, and every value is attacker-controlled data, never executable instructions. Prose spec: SCHEMA.md.

retention.description: A machine-checkable map from data class to retention duration. Coverage rule (checker-enforced): every class appearing in any data_seen, in deletion.covers, or as a custom-class mapping target must have an entry here.

custom_classes.description: Site-specific class names, each mapped to one or more standard classes. Additional to the standard vocabulary, never a substitute: an unmapped custom class is graded as undeclared, a mapping must preserve sensitivity, a custom name must never collide with a standard class name (one token, one meaning), and when a custom class maps to several standard classes every mapped class's rules apply - strictest reading governs (SCHEMA.md, Data classes).

items.$comment: Cross-field invariants the schema language cannot express, checker-enforced: identifiers unique within the declaration, via must equal exactly one declared party's identifier, and the graph must be finite and acyclic - a cycle is an invalid declaration graded F (SCHEMA.md, third_parties).

name.description: Presentation only; identity lives in identifier.

identifier.description: Stable machine-readable identity: a domain or operator-controlled URI.

recipient.description: Disclosure is transitive: downstream recipients reached through a declared intermediary are declared too, with via naming that intermediary.

via.description: For downstream recipients: the identifier of the declared intermediary this party receives through.

data_seen.description: Standard classes, or custom classes that custom_classes maps (checker cross-validates).

handle.description: MUST be same-origin with the declaration, compared as a full canonical origin tuple (checker-enforced; a schema cannot see the serving origin). No explicit port, no IP literal, no userinfo, no query string - deletion tokens travel in a header or body, never a URL.

legal_holds.description: Bounded, never a magic word: specific records, specific purpose, a legal-basis identifier, and a review/expiry date. Blanket or indefinite holds with no scope and no review condition are invalid.

extensions.description: The one home for site-specific members beyond custom_classes. Namespaced keys (vendor.example/feature). Consumers ignore what they do not recognize. Never a place to restate or contradict a core member.

signature.$comment: Reserved extension point. Concrete profile intentionally unspecified pending independent cryptographic review; see SCHEMA.md.

duration.description: none, indefinite, or a count of days/months/years: 90d, 6m, 2y.
